a.q: Tom hands the ordering of stock to his supervisor and gives her the authority to choose suppliers. Which skill is Tom using?
a.why: Tom passes a task and the authority to do it to someone else, which is delegating. Decision-making is tempting, but that is about choosing between options, not handing over a task.
a.clue: What is being handed to another person?

b.q: Zoe runs a Melbourne cafe and asks her staff for ideas before every big change. Which skill does this rely on most?

b.why: Asking staff for ideas means hearing their views, so listening is central. Planning and decision-making may happen too, but they are not what Zoe is doing when she asks for ideas.

proposal.title: Management skills
card: Communicating is passing on information clearly and listening to staff. Delegating is giving a task, and the authority to do it, to another person.
Planning is setting goals and deciding the steps and resources needed to reach them. Decision-making is choosing between options.
Leading is guiding and motivating staff. Interpersonal skills are getting on well with people, such as building trust and handling conflict.
Each management style leans on some skills more than others. A style that gives staff more say leans more on communicating and delegating.
proposal.remember: Managers use all six skills, but each style relies on some more than others.

a.why: Tom passes a task and the authority to do it to someone else, which is delegating. Decision-making is tempting, but that is choosing between options, not handing over a task.
a.clue: What is being handed to another person?

b.q: Zoe runs a Melbourne café and asks her staff for ideas before every big change. Which skill does this rely on most?
b.why: Asking staff for ideas means listening to their views, which is part of communicating. Decision-making is tempting because Zoe makes the final choice later, but asking for ideas is not choosing between options. She is not handing over a task, so it is not delegating.
b.clue: Which skill includes listening to staff?
